page: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered specifically for large-scale machine learning inference workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8275CL processors based on the x86_64 architecture. System memory consists of 192 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. The primary processing power for machine learning tasks is delivered by 16 AWS Inferentia accelerator chips equipped with a collective 128 GB of accelerator memory.

The instance does not include integrated local instance storage, requiring persistent data to be served via network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or external storage volumes. To support heavy inter-node communication and streaming data pipelines, AWS inf1.24xlarge features a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. CPU vector calculations benefit from support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions, alongside standard cryptographic and bit manipulation extensions.

Benchmark data displays strong throughput across multi-threaded computational and memory-intensive metrics. The platform achieved high marks in stress-ng multi-core execution (94571.8) and PassMark CPU evaluations (62408.52), accompanied by notable large-block uncached read speeds of 232.48 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput attained 79.6 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations scored 22949.83. Conversely, single-core evaluations show average metrics, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1284.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1561.5.

Cost efficiency is maximized when running optimized inference models targeted directly to the AWS Neuron software development kit across its 16 accelerator chips. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the absence of attached local NVMe drives mean this server is less suited for memory-heavy databases or high-disk I/O operational pipelines. It is most effectively deployed for deep learning inference, natural language processing, computer vision deployment, and distributed machine learning model serving.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is a specialized accelerated computing instance designed for machine learning inference. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it contains 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) based on 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8275CL processors with x86_64 architecture, alongside 192 GB of DDR4 memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by 16 AWS Inferentia chips with 128 GB of total accelerator memory. Network connectivity offers a 100 Gbps baseline throughput, while local disk storage is omitted, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights strong multi-core computational power and high memory bandwidth, though single-core performance remains average. The hardware distribution provides a low ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU, optimizing resource density for model execution rather than general-purpose virtualization. AWS inf1.24xlarge is specifically suited for high-throughput machine learning inference pipelines, vision models, natural language processing services, and deep learning serving architectures.
